definition: Inoculate means to vaccinate; to introduce a vaccine to protect against disease.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word inoculate. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know inoculate should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The clinic stayed open past nine so working parents could still inoculate their toddlers before kindergarten enrollment closed.
To guard is to stand watch against the danger — protection that stops well short of inoculate, which changes the body itself.
To shield blocks the threat only while the shield holds; it still stops short of inoculate, which builds protection that stays after the needle is gone.

Vaccinate is the everyday clinical word for giving the shot, and it stays in the clinic. Inoculate names the same act more formally, and it alone moves into metaphor — you can inoculate an audience against rumor, but not vaccinate one. Both describe the dose given, not the protection gained.

Immunize claims the result: protection actually achieved, the body now able to fight the disease off. Inoculate only names the act of introducing the vaccine. A patient can be inoculated on schedule and still not be immunized, if the shot fails to take hold.
